summary: Jubilee Mountain, BC: 1957 wooden lookout lost to lightning c.1989-90, replaced by a steel tower; 2023 wildfire spared it; closed and locked by 2026.

facts.design: Steel tower that replaced a 1957 wooden timber lookout; NHLR calls the design rare in British Columbia

access.note: Tower reported closed and locked in July 2026 (Columbia Valley Pioneer); no public climbing access described

visit.trail_note: Forest service road up Jubilee Mountain reported in great shape in late September 2025; the tower itself is closed

events.note: Original lookout on a wooden timber tower (firelookout.ca)
Original wooden tower destroyed by lightning around 1989-90 (firelookout.ca gives no single year)
Steel tower erected shortly afterward; source gives no exact year, 1990 is an estimate from the 1989-90 loss
Wildfire swept a large section of Jubilee on July 31, 2023; NHLR says the tower was nearly destroyed but saved
Tower described as closed and locked in a July 2026 report

corrections.proposed: 1957 built as a wooden timber tower; steel tower erected c.1990 after lightning loss; the standing tower is the later steel one
corrections.why: The 1957 date describes the original wooden lookout, which was destroyed around 1989-90; the record does not show that the standing steel tower is a replacement

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1,678 m (5,505 ft) and firelookout.ca gives 1,671 m (5,482 ft). Not reconciled; the story reports both and the brief's 1,677.9 m follows the NHLR figure.

notes_for_editor: Replacement steel tower date (c.1990) is an estimate from 'shortly afterward'. Elevation sources disagree by 7 m. BC Forest Service is named only by NHLR; no government page was read. NHLR photo is credited to Jake Lockwood but no photo URL was captured, so no photos added. Tower is closed; the story does not encourage climbing. Two search hits (Facebook group, Kamloops KMBA page) were not read.
